coverage.target: No new audit stream and no infrastructure resource: the unit writes no audit record, so the six-month retention duty stays entirely with the existing audit-retention service, which this unit neither deploys nor configures. Its only infrastructure obligation is log hygiene (no identifier in edge URLs, no credentials or problem detail in service logs), recorded under NFR21.1
monitoring-design.md — Logs & tracing; infrastructure-specification.md — Networking (no new origin) and Shared Infrastructure (edge log format unchanged)

UI unit with server additions: no new Postgres schema, no new role, no cross-schema read, and no migration (infrastructure-specification.md — Database row). Least privilege at the data layer stays the service units'

infrastructure-specification.md — the five non-denying entry points ride the existing identity-api service and its health-gated rollout; the eight gateway declarations (six settings routes over five paths plus the two export routes) in "What must exist before this works" are proven by the gateway boundary stage in cicd-pipeline.md, together with the `route_label` arms this unit adds so the surface is visible in metrics

cicd-pipeline.md — Stage 8: the jest-axe assertions in the SPA suite are a blocking gate, so accessibility fails the build rather than a review; the release order keeps a missing route a visible retry surface rather than a broken screen
infrastructure-specification.md — both i18n catalogues ship inside the existing `web` image as hashed immutable assets; no new origin, no runtime translation service

cicd-pipeline.md — Stage 10 is a blocking `yarn size` gate (300 kB initial / 150 kB route / 150 kB stylesheet, gzip); monitoring-design.md — Metrics & KPIs records the route chunk as a build-time measurement with a build-blocking alert

monitoring-design.md — "Deliberately not collected: latency": no runtime source exists (the gateway has no latency histogram or route label, and Identity's histograms do not cover D0), so NFR2.2 is verified by the MSW request-count and state assertions plus the devtools profiling pass the requirements already name; infrastructure-specification.md — Infrastructure Services records the gateway's `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS: 2000` as the server-side ceiling
Panel independence is a client-side rendering property (nfr-design/performance-design.md §3) with no infrastructure surface: the SPA is static files served by the existing nginx host
Pending-state feedback is client-side (performance-design.md §4); no infrastructure resource or configuration carries it
Single-flight destructive actions are client behaviour (performance-design.md §4, §6); the server-side `409`/`410` answers ride the existing identity-api deployment unchanged
Recovery-banner rendering is client-side (performance-design.md §3); no infrastructure resource carries it
Retry policy is the SPA query client's configuration (performance-design.md §5), shipped in the `web` bundle; no infrastructure resource carries it

cicd-pipeline.md — "What must exist before this unit can ship" lists D1's pinned no-record problem type with the two stages (4 server rendering, 8 client mapping) that prove it; the sentinel is a Contract Design dependency named in security-design.md §14.4
Cache freshness is client configuration (performance-design.md §7) in the `web` bundle; no server-side cache, proxy cache or CDN rule is involved

infrastructure-specification.md — Networking: browser reaches only the TLS edge and the gateway on `/v1` same-origin; Egress row records that this unit adds no new browser-external origin and no CSP entry
infrastructure-specification.md — Storage: no client-side storage, the query cache is memory-only, and both `web` and `identity-api` run `read_only: true` with tmpfs scratch paths
The SPA never decodes the JWT (security-design.md §3); whether a token is validated is identity-api middleware that this unit does not change
Authorisation travels as a bearer header, so no CSRF token or cookie policy is added (security-design.md §3); no infrastructure resource carries it

cicd-pipeline.md — Stage 4 asserts D3's 6th request in a window answers `429` at the gateway boundary; infrastructure-specification.md — Resource sizing records the 5/min per-token budget, with its per-replica caveat (the bucket is an in-memory fixed window in each of the gateway's 2 replicas and resets on restart, so it bounds abuse rather than enforcing an exact quota)

monitoring-design.md — Metrics & KPIs and Alerts: a sustained 429 stream on D3 is a P3 investigate signal; the client renders it as a recoverable inline error and no mutation is auto-retried, so the deployment cannot be made to amplify its own limit

monitoring-design.md — Logs & tracing: the unit holds no audit content, so its infrastructure obligation is log hygiene only — no credentials, tokens or problem detail in service logs, no identifiers in edge URLs

monitoring-design.md — Logs & tracing: nginx logs the URL and never request headers, and every settings route is self-scoped, so a user id, email or subject cannot appear in the edge log; the one id-bearing path is the opaque, ownership-checked export job id
cicd-pipeline.md — Secrets in CI/CD: no stage reads a credential into a build and no secret appears in build output; monitoring-design.md — no settings field is logged
monitoring-design.md — Logs & tracing: service logs carry no `ProblemDetails.detail`, matching the on-screen rule
Display-name rendering and its escaping are client-side (security-design.md §5); no infrastructure resource carries it
The delete page collects no free text, so there is no input for an infrastructure control to validate; the route shape is recorded under NFR22.1
Retained categories are server-reported text rendered client-side (security-design.md §5); no infrastructure resource carries it

infrastructure-specification.md — Infrastructure Services: D0/D1/D2 are handlers on the existing identity-api (3 replicas, existing pool and JWT validation), released through the health-gated rolling update; no new service, port or credential

infrastructure-specification.md — "What must exist before this works": the six settings route declarations (D0, P1, P2, D1, D2, D3 — five paths) are the enforcement point for the non-denying entry points, and cicd-pipeline.md Stage 4 proves each resolves rather than 404ing at the deny-by-default table. `GET /v1/privacy/deletions/{deletionId}` is not among them: no screen in this unit calls it
Server-decides/browser-presents is enforced in code paths this unit does not re-deploy differently; the infrastructure consequence (all calls through the gateway) is recorded under NFR9.1

infrastructure-specification.md — Database and Rollback: ownership is enforced inside identity-api against the existing schema and role; the rollback path loses no user data because preferences and deletion requests are server rows and the client cache is memory-only
Confirmation interaction is client-side (security-design.md §8); no infrastructure resource carries it
Recovery-window rendering is client-side (security-design.md §8); the server value comes from the existing identity-api deployment

infrastructure-specification.md — Infrastructure Services and Resource sizing: the bounds are enforced by the existing identity-api and gateway deployments (JWT validation, stored-record lookup, the 5/min D3 budget); no new control plane is introduced
Keyboard, heading and navigation semantics are client-side (security-design.md §12), proven by the jest-axe gate recorded under NFR25.6
Switch semantics and non-colour-only state are client-side (security-design.md §12); no infrastructure resource carries them
Error association and live-region feedback are client-side (security-design.md §12); no infrastructure resource carries them
Focus trapping is client-side (security-design.md §8); no infrastructure resource carries it
Status pill labelling and shape are client-side (security-design.md §12); no infrastructure resource carries them
cicd-pipeline.md — Stage 8 runs the SPA suite including jest-axe as a blocking gate, so an accessibility regression fails the change rather than reaching a review

infrastructure-specification.md — Shared Infrastructure: the EN and VI catalogues ship as static assets in the existing `web` image, served from the hashed immutable `/assets/` path; no new origin and no runtime translation dependency

Locale resolution order is client-side and unchanged (security-design.md §12); the stored preference persists server-side through the existing identity-api, which this unit deploys unchanged in that respect
Date and number formatting goes through `Intl` in the browser (security-design.md §12); no server-side locale resource is involved
